coding.note: Coded only the supplied report, without verifying its identifier or authenticity. C1 includes the introduced model family, architectural/optimization upgrades, distinct introductory infrastructure contributions, post-training paradigm, and headline context/efficiency/performance contributions. No element-specific ARCH/TRAIN ablations are reported; comparisons between V3.2 and V4 change architecture, data, scale, and tokens together and do not isolate these elements. Training seeds are not stated; sampling multiple solutions is not independent training replication. Comparator names are from main Table 6. Authors explicitly rerun long-context comparators and base models, but provenance and same-harness evaluation of all Table 6 scores are not established, so overall rerun and copied-score status are NR. GDPval-AA scores and a Codeforces leaderboard mention do not explicitly establish an independent evaluation run; third_party is conservatively NO. Inference FLOPs are not training-compute disclosure. Data categories are disclosed without reconstructible source proportions. Prior named techniques are adopted or modified, not explicitly renamed.

claims.claim: Introduce the DeepSeek-V4-Pro and DeepSeek-V4-Flash model family at trillion/hundred-billion parameter scales.
claims.quote:
series, including the preview versions of DeepSeek-V4-Pro with 1.6T parameters (49B activated)
and DeepSeek-V4-Flash with 284B parameters (13B activated).

claims.claim: Efficient native support for million-token contexts.
claims.quote:
This breakthrough enables efficient support for a context length of one
million tokens, ushering in a new era of million-length contexts for next-generation LLMs.

claims.claim: Hybrid attention combining Compressed Sparse Attention and Heavily Compressed Attention.
claims.quote:
context efficiency, we design a hybrid attention mechanism combining Compressed Sparse
Attention (CSA) and Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA).

claims.claim: Incorporate manifold-constrained hyper-connections to strengthen residual connections.
claims.quote:
To strengthen modeling capability, we incorporate Manifold-Constrained
Hyper-Connections (mHC) (Xie et al., 2026) that upgrade conventional residual connections.

claims.claim: Introduce Muon optimization for faster convergence and training stability.
claims.quote:
Additionally, we introduce the Muon (Jordan et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025) optimizer to the
training of DeepSeek-V4 series, leading to faster convergence and improved training stability.

claims.claim: Single fused MoE kernel overlapping computation, communication, and memory access.
claims.quote:
First, we design and implement
a single fused kernel for MoE modules that fully overlaps computation, communication, and
memory access.

claims.claim: Employ TileLang to balance kernel-development productivity and runtime efficiency.
claims.quote:
Second, we employ TileLang (Wang et al., 2026), a Domain-Specific Language
(DSL) to balance development productivity and runtime efficiency.

claims.claim: Provide efficient batch-invariant deterministic kernel libraries for bitwise reproducibility.
claims.quote:
Third, we provide efficient
batch-invariant and deterministic kernel libraries to ensure bitwise reproducibility across train-
ing and inference.

claims.claim: Extend autograd with tensor-level activation checkpointing for fine-grained recomputation control.
claims.quote:
Fourth, for the training framework, we extend the autograd framework with
tensor-level checkpointing for fine-grained recomputation control;

claims.claim: Hybrid ZeRO strategy to implement Muon efficiently.
claims.quote:
and we enhance training
efficiency with a hybrid ZeRO strategy for the Muon optimizer,

claims.quote:

claims.claim: Heterogeneous KV-cache structure and on-disk storage for efficient shared-prefix reuse.
claims.quote:
Fifth, for the inference framework, we design a heterogeneous KV cache
structure with on-disk storage strategies to enable efficient shared-prefix reuse.

claims.claim: FP4 quantization-aware post-training of expert weights and indexer QK path to reduce computation and memory.
claims.quote:
during the post-training stage, we incorporate FP4 quantization-aware training for MoE expert
weights and the indexer QK path to reduce memory and computation.

claims.claim: Substantially reduced inference FLOPs and KV-cache requirements versus DeepSeek-V3.2 at million-token context.
claims.quote:
V4-Pro requires only 27% of single-token inference FLOPs and 10% of KV cache compared
  with DeepSeek-V3.2.

claims.claim: Two-stage post-training paradigm: train domain specialists and consolidate by on-policy distillation.
claims.quote:
The post-training pipeline of DeepSeek-V4 series features a two-stage paradigm: the inde-
pendent cultivation of domain-specific experts, followed by unified model consolidation via
on-policy distillation

claims.claim: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max sets a new state of the art for open models.
claims.quote:
Max, the maximum reasoning effort mode of DeepSeek-V4-Pro, redefines the state-of-the-art for
  open models, outperforming its predecessors in core tasks.

data_disclosure.quote:
Combining all the above, our pre-training corpus comprises more than 32T tokens, containing
mathematical contents, codes, web pages, long documents, and other high-quality categories.

tokens_disclosed.quote:
During pre-training, we train DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 32T tokens and DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 33T
tokens, respectively.
